title: Ireland Stun T20 World Champions India With Historic 2-0 Series Sweep in Belfast
excerpt: Jai Moondra and Matt Hollard dismantle India's batting lineup as Ireland secure their first-ever T20 victory and series win over the reigning world champions.
body:
• Ireland defeated India by one run in the second T20I in Belfast to complete a 2-0 series sweep — their first-ever T20 victory and series win over India
  • Jai Moondra (3-32) and Matt Hollard (3-26) dismantled India's batting lineup, with player-of-the-series Moondra dismissing both Indian openers in the first over
  • India, the reigning T20 world champions and the No. 1 ranked T20I side, suffered their first T20 series defeat since January 2024
  • The result marks the first time India have lost a T20I to Ireland and raises questions about squad rotation ahead of the 2027 World Cup cycle

A Thrilling One-Run Finish

Ireland completed one of the biggest upsets in T20 cricket history on Sunday, defeating India by a single run in Belfast to clinch a 2-0 series sweep over the reigning T20 world champions. It was Ireland's first-ever T20 International victory over India, and they achieved it twice in three days.

Put in to bat on a rain-disrupted afternoon, Ireland posted 154-8, anchored by Harry Tector's composed 53 and Ben Calitz's quickfire 37. The total looked modest, but Ireland's bowling attack had other ideas.

Moondra and Hollard Wreak Havoc

Jai Moondra, who took three wickets in the first match, was devastating again. He dismissed Indian openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma in the very first over, then bowled captain Shreyas Iyer in the third, leaving India reeling at 19-3.

Matt Hollard matched Moondra's impact with three wickets of his own, including the crucial dismissal of Tilak Varma, who had fought a lone battle with 55 off 46 balls. Varma's wicket effectively ended India's realistic hopes, though Harshit Rana's cameo of 21 off 10 balls brought the visitors agonizingly close.

"I challenged the lads the other day to show the world that the first win wasn't a one-off. We have a lot of lads with very few caps but they showed great character. It is a great time to be a professional cricketer in Ireland."

— Lorcan Tucker, Ireland captain

India needed eight runs from the last two balls. Rana swung for the boundary but was caught by Tim Tector off Harry Tector's bowling, sealing Ireland's historic series victory.

What Went Wrong for India

India arrived in Belfast as the world's top-ranked T20I side and defending world champions, but their performance suggested a team in transition. Captain Shreyas Iyer became the fourth Indian captain — after Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant, and Shubman Gill — to lose his maiden T20I in charge.

The series exposed vulnerabilities in India's middle order and raised questions about the depth behind their first-choice players. Several key names were rested for the tour, and the results suggest India's reserves lack the match-hardness needed to compete even against lower-ranked opposition.

"Kudos to them, the way they played. They showed professionalism, they had tremendous idea of how the wicket was going to play," Iyer acknowledged after the defeat.

Ireland's Rising Ambitions

For Cricket Ireland, the result validates years of investment in developing domestic talent. Board Chair Brian MacNeice told Cricbuzz that the victory was "a very, very significant milestone" and pledged that Ireland's ambition extends beyond one-off upsets.

"Our target is to qualify for all ICC competitions, both men's and women's. We don't just want to qualify — we want to be able to compete when we're there," MacNeice said. He pointed to the European T20 Premier League as a critical platform for giving Irish players consistent exposure to high-level competition.

India's struggles continued after leaving Belfast. They headed to England for a five-match T20 series starting July 1 and have since failed to win a single match, trailing 3-0 in the series — an extended slump that began with Ireland's stunning breakthrough in Belfast.
